audit: Issue #233 — full repository reachability and dead-artifact audit
scope_note: Read-only. Nothing outside reports/repository_audit/** and docs/repository-audit/** was modified. Nothing was published, no provider call was made, no CONTROLLED_LIVE run was started. Discovery of a defect here does not authorize its repair: each finding below names the narrowly scoped follow-up it wants.
counts_note: 7,824 of the 7,844 DEAD_ORPHANED paths are the two test-run-record groups plus the card-audit renders (F-02, F-02b). Outside reports/, DEAD_ORPHANED is 20 paths. Both high-risk classes — PRODUCT_CONFIG_UNWIRED_PARTIAL (14) and SUSPICIOUS_UNRESOLVED (2) — carry one entry per path; neither appears in any paths_file group.
counts_revision_note: These counts were revised after a review of this audit's own method, and the revision is recorded rather than silently applied. Five reclassifications, all in the same direction — the earlier pass had treated a refused loader or a missing workflow as proof of absent purpose, which it is not. (1) docs/NEVER_BLANK_GOLDEN_EDITORIAL_PATTERNS.md: DUPLICATE_SUPERSEDED -> PRODUCT_CONFIG_UNWIRED_PARTIAL — nothing supersedes it, and the claim that the three Wednesday artifacts carry no cross-reference was false: that document names both machine artifacts at :19-22. (2) config/prompts/{image_hook,strategy_brief,topic_score}.yaml: DEAD_ORPHANED -> LEGACY_INTENTIONAL — each states in its own text that it is retained to document an architectural decision, and its loader's refusal is the mechanism that keeps it inert, not evidence that it is purposeless. (3) scripts/{dry_run,render_card_audit}.py: DEAD_ORPHANED -> LEGACY_INTENTIONAL — both document their own manual invocation; having no workflow is not having no consumer. (4) reports/content_packages/<sig>_generated.json (8 paths): LEGACY_INTENTIONAL -> ACTIVE_SUPPORT — they are current output of research Stage 11 with a live reader, not legacy input to a fallback that cannot execute (F-15). (5) reports/content_packages/vis_00N_generated.json (6 paths): LEGACY_INTENTIONAL -> ACTIVE_SUPPORT — justified by the tracked history entries that name each path, not by a resume flag that does not exist (F-15).

findings.title: A live Friday cron reaches a six-channel publisher that no allowlist covers, and the only thing stopping it is a YAML parse error
findings.what: scheduled_publish.yml fires every Friday at 08:17 and 09:17 UTC. It runs scripts/scheduled_publish.py, which at :226-240 shells out with subprocess to scripts/generate.py --qc, scripts/generate_image.py --upload, and then scripts/publish.py --live --channels <ch> for wix, linkedin, facebook, instagram, threads and telegram. scripts/publish.py:50-58 maps all six publishers and imports none of src/publishing/release_scope.py. Neither does scripts/generate.py or scripts/scheduled_publish.py. The #229 allowlist governs the canonical entrypoint, the visibility publisher and research Stage 11 — not this path.
findings.why_it_has_not_fired: Step 1 is abort_on_fail=True and it aborts: src/content/generator.py:134 calls load_prompt('linkedin_post'), and config/prompts/linkedin_post.yaml does not parse. Lines 63-67 put ' #success' and ' #PresenceDebt)' inside block-sequence scalars, where a space-preceded '#' opens a YAML comment. Three independent in-repo records state the failure — tests/test_cross_platform_overlap_policy.py:312-320, the #234 forensic §4, and the owner's verification comment of 2026-09-15, which quotes the PyYAML error.
findings.why_it_matters: A parse error is not a control. It fails in front of generation, not in front of publication, and it can be removed by anyone who thinks they are fixing a broken file. The owner recorded this exactly on 2026-09-15: 'The invalid YAML is not an accepted safety mechanism. It is what currently prevents publication, and it is a defect standing in for a control that does not exist.'
findings.not_verified_here: I could not execute a YAML parse in this environment (no Python execution available), so the parse failure rests on the three repository records above plus the readable mechanism at :63-67, not on a run I performed.
findings.follow_up: One narrowly scoped issue: put a real control in front of the Friday path. The options are (a) disable the scheduled_publish.yml cron while Friday is paused, (b) make scripts/publish.py import and honour release_scope, or (c) both. Do NOT repair config/prompts/linkedin_post.yaml as part of it — the owner has already ruled that repairing it re-enables the publisher.

findings.title: 7,796 of the repository's 8,392 tracked files (92.9%) are test-run debris
findings.what: reports/content_packages/sig-test-001/runs/<uuid>/ and reports/content_packages/sig-identity-test-001/runs/<uuid>/ hold 4,702 and 3,094 files respectively, plus the two flat sig-*.json packages. Across both namespaces there are exactly six distinct basenames — business_strategy.json (2,422), generated.json (2,263), editorial_acceptance.json (1,343), assignment.json (1,263), publication_results.json (469), run_report.json (36) — one set per test execution of the canonical entrypoint.
findings.mechanism: scripts/generate_and_publish.py:320 defines PACKAGES_DIR as the RELATIVE path reports/content_packages and :321 mkdirs it at import time. :1052 calls resolve_run_dir(PACKAGES_DIR, signal_id, run_ctx.run_id), creating one directory per fresh uuid4 run id. tests/conftest.py isolates OpenAI credentials and does not isolate the filesystem, so any test that exercises the entrypoint without redirecting PACKAGES_DIR writes into the real tree. Nothing under reports/ is ignored except reports/content_packages/images/ (.gitignore:27).
findings.how_they_entered_and_why_it_keeps_costin: They entered in one commit: ffe199a (2026-08-17), 7,830 files and 917,551 insertions, whose subject is a 69-line change to src/reporting/run_report.py. They keep re-entering: dd54dc5 (#223) — a two-line message change in src/utils/config_loader.py — shipped 145 files and 864 insertions/deletions, all of it this debris, and the same happened on its two rebases (299e747, 39043ea). Every future diff that follows a local test run carries this noise, which is exactly how a real change hides.
findings.the_question_the_issue_asks: Do ~8,000 tracked run records belong in source control? Split the answer. The 7,796 test-run records: no. They have no consumer, no product meaning and an active cost. The four real run-record groups — 63 daily research reports, 47 per-signal packages, 8 flat generated packages, 6 visibility packages: yes for now. Their tracking is deliberate and expressed in the workflows that commit them (daily_signal_research.yml:106, visibility_publish.yml:102), each has a producer and a demonstrated consumer (see 09_reports.json), and src/run/code_identity.py:34-43 states the repository's position that reports/ is an output root a run legitimately dirties. What those four groups lack is a retention policy, not a justification.
evidence: tests/test_research_artifact_lifecycle.py:371-541 — the correct pattern, PACKAGES_DIR redirected to tmp_path
findings.follow_up: One narrowly scoped issue: git rm -r --cached the two test namespaces, add them to .gitignore using the same explicit named pattern data/ already uses, and add an autouse fixture (or a per-suite one) that points PACKAGES_DIR at tmp_path so the situation cannot recur. Then decide a retention policy for the two legitimate groups.

findings.title: reports/card_audit/ is tracked against an explicitly recorded decision that it stay untracked
findings.what: 26 PNGs (3.1 MB) produced by scripts/render_card_audit.py for one human before/after comparison. No test, script, workflow or document reads them, and the script itself has no workflow.
findings.why_it_matters: strategy/decision_log.md decision 97 (2026-08-07) records the owner's decision verbatim: reports/card_audit/ is deliberately left untracked, 26 PNG, 3.1 MB, not added to .gitignore and not committed, 'статус untracked сохраняется до отдельного решения'. The Часть 22 status line repeats it. Ten days later ffe199a committed all 26. This is the decision log being contradicted by the repository — the one place where that must not happen, because the log is the record of truth.
evidence: strategy/decision_log.md decision 97 and the Часть 22 closing status line
findings.follow_up: Bundle with F-02: untrack and ignore, restoring decision 97 — or supersede decision 97 with a new recorded decision. The current state is neither.

findings.title: Ten declared-authoritative product/editorial artifacts reach no production prompt; two of them are declared executable and one of them used to be
findings.what: For every artifact below the required chain file -> loader -> prompt/profile composition -> production model-message construction is broken at the first link: no loader in the repository can read Markdown as configuration. src/utils/config_loader.py:11,38 read YAML; src/strategy/business_config.py:272 reads JSON. Every .md read in src/ or scripts/ is a report being written.
artifacts: config/brand_voice.md — registered at business_strategy.json:313-314 as prompt_rule_reference 'brand-voice' version r1-2026-08-13; never opened

docs/NEVER_BLANK_EDITORIAL_STYLE.md — WAS runtime until commit 2466611 (2026-07-03), when scripts/research/publish_packages._load_editorial_style() was deleted along with the prompt that used it; the commit message does not mention it, and no test referenced the document or the loader, so nothing could turn red. Quoted in full, with the reproducing commands, in reports/repository_audit/evidence/EDITORIAL_STYLE_DISCONNECTION.md
docs/NEVER_BLANK_EDITORIAL_WORLDVIEW.md — claims to be the document all prompts follow from; not registered anywhere and not read
docs/PLATFORM_AND_VISUAL_STRATEGY.md — registered at business_strategy.json:338-339; never opened; its numbers contradict the running code
strategy/methodology/strategy_methodology.md — registered twice (business_strategy.json:323-324 and strategy.json:58); never opened
strategy/methodology/platform_strategy.md — registered at business_strategy.json:333-334; never opened
strategy/methodology/evaluation_rules.md — 'Status: Production' and not registered anywhere at all
strategy/worldview.md — registered at strategy.json:59 as a research_reference; never opened
strategy/current/strategy.md — a hand-maintained Markdown twin of strategy.json, which the owner's 2026-09-15 ruling forbids
findings.why_ci_allowed_it: tests/strategy/test_never_blank_business_config.py:80 test_all_prompt_and_rule_references_resolve_inside_repository asserts resolved.is_file(). A reference no code opens passes that test forever. src/strategy/business_config.py:187-191 validates the id, path and version strings; src/strategy/validators.py:47-55 requires research_references to be present and non-empty. Identity was wired (tests/strategy/test_configuration_hash_snapshot.py); content never was.
findings.what_reaches_a_prompt_instead: Thirteen of the fifteen model calls on the Monday path take their system prompt from a Python string constant. The two exceptions are the editorial reviewer and reviser, which read config/prompts/editorial_acceptance/never_blank.yaml. Fragments of brand_voice.md, STYLE and WORLDVIEW were hand-copied into src/editorial/{narrative_spine,hook_engine,pattern_extractor}.py once, inconsistently, with no link, version or test, and have drifted.
conflicts_that_must_be_resolved_before_a: blog length: code and business_strategy.json:237 say 400-600; docs/PLATFORM_AND_VISUAL_STRATEGY.md:27 says 700-1000; strategy/methodology/platform_strategy.md:30 says 600-1200
article arc: four different arcs across src/editorial/platform_composer.py:121-122, config/brand_voice.md:262-265, docs/NEVER_BLANK_EDITORIAL_STYLE.md:48-60 and business_strategy.json:347-358
hashtags: here the CODE is right and config/brand_voice.md:200-201 is stale — which is why one source must win per rule, not per file
evidence: reports/repository_audit/evidence/EDITORIAL_STYLE_DISCONNECTION.md — the STYLE chain before 2466611, the deletion, and the greps showing no test referenced it
`git log --oneline -S brand_voice -- src scripts` is empty: config/brand_voice.md was never wired, not unwired
the thirteen Python-constant system prompts, each cited by file and line in reports/repository_audit/inventory/03_src.json
findings.follow_up: This audit does not propose the repair; #240/#244 already own it and are blocked on owner rulings. What this audit adds is the guardrail: G-2 below, which must exist before any of these documents is declared wired again.
findings.do_not_do: Do not edit any of these ten artifacts, and do not make the #231 product choice implicitly.

findings.title: Wednesday's configured Golden contract exists three times and reaches generation zero times, and the test that says otherwise exercises a constructor production no longer uses
findings.what: config/never_blank/wednesday_golden.yaml holds the nine-stage reasoning movement, the editorial prohibitions (including the 'no 5 lessons / 3 takeaways' bans), the title contract, text shape and source policy. Its loader src/never_blank/wednesday_golden.py executes in production — src/never_blank/__init__.py:7 re-exports it, so scripts/generate_and_publish.py:175 imports it transitively — but no production call site ever invokes WednesdayGoldenProfile.load(), source_eligibility_rules() or generation_rules(). The only callers are tests/test_wednesday_golden.py:146,496.
findings.what_generation_actually_receives: scripts/generate_and_publish.py:1880 calls generate_for_wednesday(editorial.to_legacy_dict()) — the signal dict and nothing else. No strategy, no role rules, no channel rules, no CTA, no closing contract, no sources block. src/never_blank/wednesday_july/platform_composer.compose_platforms takes one argument. _editorial_role_rules IS computed for Wednesday at :920 and then not passed. #210 disclosed this; the deviation was accepted, not hidden.
findings.why_ci_allowed_it: tests/test_wednesday_golden.py:397 test_golden_rules_reach_the_existing_wix_and_linkedin_prompt_constructor builds prompts with the SHARED src/editorial/platform_composer._build_user_prompt. Since #210 Wednesday generation uses src/never_blank/wednesday_july/platform_composer.compose_platforms. The test was not retargeted when production moved, so it still passes while the contract it names is unmet. grep for '5 lessons' or '3 takeaways' over src/never_blank/wednesday_july/ finds nothing.
findings.the_three_copies: config/never_blank/wednesday_golden.yaml (machine), docs/NEVER_BLANK_GOLDEN_EDITORIAL_PATTERNS.md (2026-08-20, self-declared 'Release 1 product configuration'), docs/product/wednesday_golden_contract.md (2026-09-05). Exactly one cross-reference exists, and it runs from the 2026-08-20 document outward: :19-22 names the YAML profile as 'the machine-readable product profile' and config/prompts/editorial_acceptance/never_blank_golden_wednesday.yaml as its acceptance artifact. Nothing points the other way, and the 2026-09-05 contract names neither the others nor either machine copy. So there is no supersession in either direction — what is missing is an authority statement, not a reference. Neither prose document is read by production; of the two machine artifacts the profile is unread and the rubric is wired. The rubric path and identity are additionally duplicated between the YAML (:10-11) and business_strategy.json:442-443, and only the JSON copy is honoured.
findings.blocked_on: The owner decision between July byte-fidelity (#207/#210, enforced by the byte-fidelity fixtures in tests/fixtures/wednesday_july/july_originals/) and the configured Golden contract. Wednesday is architecturally paused (#234 comment, 2026-09-15) while its schedule keeps running.
findings.follow_up: Nothing to repair now. Two things can be done without touching the product decision: (1) retarget or explicitly xfail tests/test_wednesday_golden.py:397 so CI stops reporting a contract that is not met; (2) name one source of truth among the three Golden artifacts (see F-14).
findings.do_not_do: Do not change Wednesday architecture, prompts, generation, acceptance or semantics.

findings.title: Friday has two scheduled publishers, and the Research Full LLM Fri/Sun path publishes with no editorial role at all
findings.what: research_generate_and_publish.yml fires at 07:00 UTC on Friday and Sunday (:34); scheduled_publish.yml fires at 08:17/09:17 UTC on Friday (:23-24). They are different entrypoints with different semantics publishing the same brand on the same day. The Research path auto-selects a signal from signals_active.jsonl (:57-85) and calls scripts/generate_and_publish.py with NO --editorial-role (:170).
findings.what_no_role_means: scripts/generate_and_publish.py:1286 requires _role.decision_policy == 'role_bounded_r1' to take the role-bounded branch. With no role there is no branch to take: the run falls to the Decision Lens, and none of the Never Blank editorial role rules, surface rules or source-transparency requirements apply. Monday and Wednesday are the two configured Never Blank products; this path publishes a third thing that no role describes.
findings.secondary: Its 'Check publish secrets' step is skipped on every scheduled run, because it is guarded by `if: inputs.dry_run == 'false'` (:100) and `inputs` is empty on a cron. So the scheduled path has no secret preflight at all.
findings.the_question_the_issue_asks: Publication ownership of the Research Full LLM Fri/Sun path is undecided in the repository. The workflow comment at :30-33 asserts 'Monday and Wednesday are owned by their independent canonical streams. Friday and Sunday remain unchanged here' — written before the #229 scope work and before Friday was paused. The owner's 2026-09-15 note says Research publication stays disabled and #238 stays unmerged; the cron in this file is nevertheless live and this path is not what #238 gates.
findings.follow_up: An owner decision, not a code change: does the Fri/Sun Research path publish, and if so under which editorial role? Until that is answered, the safe intermediate step is to disable its cron, which is one line and reversible.

findings.title: Three publishing workflows have no concurrency group and push the same two state files
findings.what: monday_publish.yml:53-55, wednesday_golden.yml:32-34 and research_generate_and_publish.yml:37-39 all declare concurrency group never-blank-publish. scheduled_publish.yml (Friday), visibility_publish.yml (Tue/Thu) and daily_signal_research.yml (daily, Stage 11 can publish) declare none.
findings.why_it_matters: data/research/published_signal_ids.txt and strategy/published_content_index.jsonl are appended and pushed by several of these. Two overlapping runs do `git pull --rebase --autostash` and push; the loser either rebases over the winner or fails. On Friday the two publishers can overlap by design (F-05).
evidence: scheduled_publish.yml (no concurrency key), visibility_publish.yml (no concurrency key), daily_signal_research.yml (no concurrency key)
findings.follow_up: Add the never-blank-publish concurrency group to the three workflows that lack it. Small, low-risk, and it belongs with F-01 or F-05 rather than on its own.

findings.title: Dead and orphaned artifacts outside reports/: 20 paths with no justified consumer

groups.name: The Strategy Engine monthly loop (9 paths)
groups.evidence: No workflow executes any of the four scripts; strategy_tests.yml:64-67 only py_compiles them, and compiling is not a consumer. build_monthly_plan.py:33 reads reports/signals/, which does not exist; content_planner.py writes strategy/current/content_plan.*, which does not exist; strategy/reviews/{weekly,monthly,recommendations}/ contain only .gitkeep. Built to the spec in strategy/claude_code_prompt_strategy_engine_FINAL_2026-07-22.md and never wired.

groups.name: Directory markers for the above (3 paths)
groups.evidence: Their only writers are the orphaned review scripts.

groups.name: The investigation layer (2 paths)
groups.evidence: No production importer. Its only consumer is tests/test_hypothesis_generator.py — a test is not a justified consumer for a module that presents itself as production code. docs/BUSINESS_INVESTIGATION_LAYER.md is its specification.

groups.name: Orphaned scripts (1 path)
groups.evidence: It is not invoked by a workflow and not imported: run_daily_research.py:31 imports only sync_to_sheets. What makes it dead rather than manual is that it declares itself 'Stage 8' of the research pipeline (:1-4) and docs/SYSTEM_MAP.md:17 and docs/NEVER_BLANK_RESEARCH_PIPELINE.md repeat that claim — a declared position in a pipeline that never calls it, not a tool an operator is told to run.

groups.name: Orphaned configuration and prompts (5 paths)
groups.evidence: config/content_matrix.yaml is shadowed by config/prompts/content_matrix.yaml and loaded by nothing. config/intelligence.yaml is loaded only from scripts/dry_run.py:82. The three observation/topic prompts are named only in scripts/dry_run.py:96-97 and all three carry status: ready, i.e. they present themselves as usable and are not. docs/SYSTEM_MAP.md:28,55-57 nevertheless presents them as live.

groups.name: Explicitly NOT in this finding, after a review of the method (5 paths)
groups.evidence: An earlier revision of this audit counted these as DEAD_ORPHANED and proposed them for deletion. That was wrong twice over, and the reasoning is recorded here so the same error is not repeated. The three prompts carry `status: not_needed`, and each says in its own text that it is kept to document an architectural decision and where the deterministic implementation lives instead (image_hook.yaml:3-7,9-17 is the clearest). Their loader's refusal — src/utils/config_loader.py:49-53 raises a ValueError quoting the file's own `decision` field — is what guarantees they cannot become an accidental active path; a disabled execution path deliberately kept disabled is the definition of LEGACY_INTENTIONAL, not of DEAD. The two scripts document their own manual invocation (dry_run.py:1-9, render_card_audit.py:1-17); no workflow is not the same as no consumer, and this audit already classifies the dispatch-only smoke tests as LEGACY_INTENTIONAL on exactly that basis. All five are reclassified LEGACY_INTENTIONAL, which is why the count here is 20 and not 25.

groups.name: The index that keeps them looking alive (1 path, classified SUSPICIOUS_UNRESOLVED, not counted in the 20)
groups.evidence: Classified SUSPICIOUS_UNRESOLVED in 06_docs.json. It describes only the V1 system: Monday, Wednesday, Visibility, the canonical entrypoint and release_scope are absent, seven of its entries name files that no code loads — including the three retained decision records at :32,:46,:58, which it presents as live prompts although their own text says they are deliberately not used — and :73 names reports/full_live_matrix_test.{json,md}, which no script writes.

findings.follow_up: Three separate small issues, in this order: (1) rewrite or retire docs/SYSTEM_MAP.md — it is cheap and it stops the wrong picture spreading; (2) one owner decision on the Strategy Engine monthly loop, then retire or wire all twelve paths together; (3) one decision each on the investigation layer and on scripts/research/sync_from_sheets.py, since both correspond to a documented capability the product may still want.
findings.do_not_do: Do not delete any of these on static-search evidence alone. Each group corresponds to a documented intention, and the issue forbids deletion on the strength of a missing import. Do not delete the five paths of the fourth group at all: their purpose is to be readable.

findings.title: The #247 one-shot recovery is still present and dispatchable past its own declared removal condition
findings.what: .github/workflows/recovery_wednesday_meta_247.yml plus scripts/recovery/{__init__,check_prior_live_runs,publish_saved_wednesday_meta}.py, tests/test_recovery_wednesday_meta.py and tests/fixtures/recovery_247/**. The workflow header (:9) and the script docstring (:39) both say to remove them after the recovery, in a separate cleanup PR. The recovery merged as 4a121b2.
findings.why_it_is_low: It is the best-contained thing in the repository: workflow_dispatch only, dry_run by default, live requires typing the source run id, read-only token, only Meta-family secrets, digest-bound to one run's evidence, and single-shot via check_prior_live_runs.py. It is also the only path that can publish to non-R1 channels by design, so it should not outlive its purpose by accident.
findings.follow_up: Track the cleanup PR the two files already ask for. Nothing to decide.

findings.title: Four name and authority collisions that make the wrong file easy to open
collisions: scripts/generate_and_publish.py (THE canonical Release 1 entrypoint, Monday/Wednesday/Research) vs .github/workflows/generate_and_publish.yml (a manual LEGACY workflow that runs generate.py + publish.py and never touches the canonical entrypoint). Identical names, opposite meanings.
config/strategy.yaml (V1 content strategy, legacy Friday path) vs strategy/current/strategy.json (the active campaign strategy, canonical path). Neither file says the other exists.
src/editorial/pattern_extractor.py (live, Monday) vs src/strategy/pattern_extractor.py (DEAD_ORPHANED). Same module name in two packages, one live and one dead.

Two schedule authorities: Monday and Wednesday decide whether to run via crons plus scripts/streams/due_check.py; Friday decides via config/schedule.yaml plus scripts/scheduled_publish.py:180. tests/test_scheduling_window.py covers only the first.
findings.follow_up: No code change required. A short ORIENTATION section in the rewritten docs/SYSTEM_MAP.md (F-07) naming the canonical entrypoint and the legacy one is the whole fix.

findings.title: Four tests report a contract as met that production does not meet

tests.proves: that each prompt_rule_reference path is a file on disk (resolved.is_file())
tests.does_not_prove: that any code opens it. This is what let config/brand_voice.md ship as a versioned prompt contract that no prompt has ever seen.

tests.proves: that generate_article was called with an editorial_role_rules argument (generate_article is patched)
tests.does_not_prove: that any model message contains them. The sibling test_the_role_reaches_composition_through_the_real_call IS a genuine capture — but only of the composer, not of the upstream stages or the reviser.

tests.proves: that the shared src/editorial/platform_composer._build_user_prompt incorporates Golden rules when given them
tests.does_not_prove: anything about Wednesday, which since #210 composes through src/never_blank/wednesday_july/platform_composer.compose_platforms — a different constructor that takes no rules. The test was not retargeted when production moved (F-04).

tests.proves: that scripts/scheduled_publish.py contains no *Publisher class name
tests.does_not_prove: that Friday reaches no channel. It shells out to scripts/publish.py, which reaches all six. The docstring's claim that Friday 'shells out to the canonical entrypoint' is wrong (F-01). The neighbouring test_manual_publishers_may_still_reach_every_channel (:213) likewise treats publish.py as manual-only while a scheduled workflow reaches it.

findings.the_general_shape: Each proves the weakest thing that is easy to assert — existence, a call signature, a constructor in isolation, the absence of a symbol — and each was true when written. Production moved underneath three of them and nothing noticed, because no test in the repository spans entrypoint to model messages. That is hard to write naively for a real reason: every stage binds chat by name (from src.utils.llm_client import chat), so patching src.utils.llm_client.chat intercepts nothing; the patch must go into each stage module's own namespace.
evidence: the four test node ids above

src/utils/llm_client.py, and the by-name binding in each stage module — src/editorial/decision_lens_lite.py:25, hook_engine.py:14, narrative_spine.py:15, story_assembly.py:18 all do `from src.utils.llm_client import chat` and then call the bare name at :184, :134, :127, :135
findings.follow_up: Guardrail G-2 below. Retargeting tests/test_wednesday_golden.py:397 can be done immediately and independently of any product decision, because it only changes what CI reports, not what Wednesday does.

findings.title: daily_signal_research.yml installs a hand-written package list instead of requirements.txt
findings.what: daily_signal_research.yml:34 runs `pip install --quiet openai PyYAML requests google-auth google-api-python-client Pillow cloudinary`. requirements.txt also pins python-dotenv, gspread, feedparser and numpy, and carries version floors.
findings.why_it_matters: The daily stream is the one that runs most often, and it runs against a different dependency set from every other workflow. feedparser in particular is an RSS library, and discovery is an RSS stage.
findings.follow_up: Fold into whichever workflow-touching issue lands first. Not worth its own PR.

findings.title: The Decision Lens is documented as the mandatory gate and is bypassed by both configured products
findings.what: docs/DECISION_LENS_CONTRACT.md, docs/DECISION_LENS_EVALUATOR.md, docs/DECISION_LIFECYCLE.md and docs/STORY_12_ACCEPTANCE.md describe the Decision Lens as the business gate between research and all downstream work. Both editorial roles declare decision_policy: role_bounded_r1 (business_strategy.json:393, :444), and scripts/generate_and_publish.py:1286-1336 takes the bypass branch for them, writing decision_policy.json instead of decision.json. In practice the Lens runs only on the role-less Fri/Sun research path.
findings.why_it_is_not_a_bug: The bypass is deliberate, typed, recorded in an artifact and verified by src/artifacts/provenance.py:261-309. What is missing is the sentence in the four documents saying so.
findings.follow_up: A documentation-only change: record the role_bounded_r1 bypass in the four documents. Independent of every product decision.

findings.title: release_scope.py claims that adding a channel is a change to one file; about twenty other places hard-code Wix and LinkedIn
findings.what: src/publishing/release_scope.py:1-25 states that adding a channel is 'a change to this file and nowhere else'. It is not. Independent Wix/LinkedIn-only lists exist at, among others: scripts/generate_and_publish.py:508 (_R1_COMPOSER_FORMATS), :509 (_R1_IMAGE_PLATFORMS), :2768 (_r1_cls), :2582-2632, :2821-2825, :2314, :3129; src/publishing/preflight.py:62-65, :226, :280, :484-492; src/visual/contract.py:44-47, :146-150, :291-309; src/reporting/run_report.py:131-136, :336, :446; src/publishing/idempotency.py:227-231, :278-305; src/strategy/business_config.py:182-184; src/strategy/execution_context.py:190-253; src/editorial/editorial_role.py:104-106; src/publishing/package.py:174-265 (no package model for any other channel).
findings.why_it_matters: Two opposite risks from one false docstring. Someone adding a channel by editing release_scope.py alone gets a run that passes the allowlist and then fails deep in preflight or packaging. Someone reading the docstring believes the allowlist is the whole control, which is how F-01 stayed invisible.
evidence: the file:line list above, each checked at the audited commit
findings.follow_up: Correct the docstring. That is the whole fix; consolidating the lists is a separate design question that #248 owns.

findings.title: Three source-of-truth conflicts with no declared winner

conflicts.subject: The Wednesday Golden contract
conflicts.state: This conflict is UNRESOLVED, not superseded, and the distinction was got wrong in an earlier revision of this audit. The 2026-08-20 document is not a stale copy: it names its own machine artifacts at :19-22 (the profile and the acceptance rubric), which is one more declared relationship than either of the others carries. The 2026-09-05 document names nothing and is named by nothing. Newer is not more authoritative, and no artifact in the repository claims authority over another. Neither prose copy is read by production; the rubric path is additionally duplicated into strategy/current/business_strategy.json:442-443, which is the only copy the runtime honours.
conflicts.provisional_source_of_truth: business_strategy.json for the rubric path. For the contract prose, NONE — and this audit deliberately does not nominate one, because choosing between the 2026-08-20 and 2026-09-05 documents is the Wednesday product decision of #234, not an editorial-hygiene call. findings.title: Two recorded retry capabilities for prepared packages do not exist: one is unreachable code, the other is a comment with no implementation
findings.classification_of_subject: ACTIVE_RUNTIME (the two entrypoints); ACTIVE_SUPPORT (the package groups they were thought to serve)
findings.what: Both flat-package groups under reports/content_packages/ were justified in an earlier revision of this audit by a resume/fallback path. Neither path exists, and the difference between what the code advertises and what it does is the finding.
findings.the_legacy_package_adapter: scripts/generate_and_publish.py accepts --legacy-package (:854-855, documented at :77-80 and :98) and can never use it. The branch structure is `if not args.from_package and not args.legacy_package:` (:1174) ... `elif args.legacy_package:` (:1380), and that elif prints 'legacy prepared packages have no canonical research lineage' and returns 1 (:1381-1382). Since the elif is reached on exactly the condition that would make the flag meaningful, the loader beneath it at :1407-1421 — which opens PACKAGES_DIR / f'{signal_id}_generated.json' — is unreachable in every execution. --from-package is a different flag and does not fall back: :1391-1394 returns 1 when the run-scoped generated.json is missing.
findings.the_visibility_resume: scripts/generate_and_publish_visibility.py:425 comments that it saves the package 'for audit trail + --from-package retry'. The audit-trail half is real (:479 records the path into visibility_history.jsonl). The retry half is not: main() at :344-347 defines only --item-id and --dry-run, there is no --from-package flag, and the script never reads a package back — the only PACKAGES_DIR uses are the mkdir at :63, the DraftPackage draft_dir at :254 and the write at :426-427.
findings.why_it_matters: Neither is a live defect — no run takes either path, which is why this is low. It matters because both were read as evidence that a tracked artifact was retained on purpose, and both times the artifact turned out to have a different and better justification: current Stage 11 output with a live reader for the flat packages, and the tracked history pointer for the visibility packages. An advertised capability is not a consumer. The corrected entries are in reports/repository_audit/inventory/09_reports.json.
evidence: scripts/research/publish_packages.py:288 (the real producer of the flat packages)
findings.follow_up: Documentation-sized, and it belongs with F-13 in the docs-only issue: either make --legacy-package do what its help text says, or remove the flag and the unreachable loader with it; and correct the comment at generate_and_publish_visibility.py:425 to claim only the audit trail. Both are behaviour-preserving as written.
findings.do_not_do: Do not implement a resume capability under this issue. Establishing that it is absent is the audit's job; adding it is a product change nobody asked for.

guardrails.name: Configuration parse gate
guardrails.rule_it_serves: A config artifact that cannot be loaded is not DONE.
guardrails.proposal: Add one test, tests/test_config_loads.py, that walks every tracked config/**/*.yaml plus strategy/current/*.json and asserts each one loads. Prompts carrying status: not_needed are asserted to raise the specific ValueError from src/utils/config_loader.py:49-53 rather than a parse error, so the two failure modes stay distinguishable. It runs inside the existing pr_tests.yml full-suite gate; no new workflow, no new dependency.
guardrails.would_have_caught: config/prompts/linkedin_post.yaml, at the commit that broke it, years of Fridays ago in pipeline time.

guardrails.name: Sentinel wiring test for declared-executable product artifacts
guardrails.rule_it_serves: An authoritative product/config artifact intended to influence model output must have a regression test proving that a distinctive instruction reaches the actual production model-message construction.
guardrails.proposal: One test module, tests/test_product_config_reaches_prompts.py. For each artifact declared executable (the prompt_rule_references block of strategy/current/business_strategy.json, minus any entry explicitly marked authoring-only), it (a) copies the artifact to a temp path with a unique sentinel string inserted, (b) points the loader at the copy, (c) runs the production entrypoint for the relevant role with `chat` patched in EACH stage module's own namespace — not in src.utils.llm_client, because every stage binds it by name — recording (module, system, user) for every call, and (d) asserts the sentinel appears in at least one recorded message, naming which stage. The 'which stage' assertion is the point: a future move of a rule between stages then becomes a visible decision rather than a silent one.
guardrails.cost: one module, and a required `authoring_only: true` flag on prompt_rule_references entries that are not executable — a two-line schema change in src/strategy/business_config.py
guardrails.would_have_caught: the deletion of _load_editorial_style() in 2466611, and would fail today for config/brand_voice.md, which is exactly the signal wanted.
guardrails.note: This deliberately replaces, rather than supplements, tests/strategy/test_never_blank_business_config.py:80's is_file() assertion for executable entries. Existence stays the test for authoring-only entries.

guardrails.name: Tracked-path classification manifest
guardrails.rule_it_serves: Unjustified orphaned production artifacts are not allowed; intentional human-only documentation must be clearly distinguishable.
guardrails.proposal: Keep one tracked file, reports/repository_audit/inventory/*.json (this audit's own output), as the live manifest, and add a test that every tracked path outside the audit directories matches exactly one entry or paths_file group. A new file then fails CI until someone writes one line saying what it is for and who consumes it. Deliberately NOT a reachability analyser: the assertion is that a human classified the path, not that a tool proved it — the tool would be wrong about dynamic loading and would teach people to route around it.
guardrails.cost: about 40 lines plus the discipline of maintaining the manifest; the manifest already exists as of this audit.
guardrails.caveat: This only pays for itself if the bulk groups stay groups. If reports/ keeps accumulating run records the manifest must address them by paths_file, which is why F-02's retention policy is a prerequisite rather than a nice-to-have.
